title: We built an AI news desk that writes in Bangla twice a day, clusters duplicate stories, and credits every source
summary:
Most AI news in Bangla is either a translated headline with no context or a copied article. We wanted something closer to a morning newsletter: what happened, why it matters, and what it changes for someone working in Bangladesh, written in Bangla that reads like a person wrote it.

So our academy runs its own small news desk:

  1. A collector checks a list of tech and AI news sources every 30 minutes and scores each headline.
  2. Two editorial runs a day, at 8 AM and 7 PM Dhaka time, the way a newspaper has a morning and an evening edition. Each run writes at most three stories.
  3. The bar rises for each extra story. The first story only needs to clear a basic score. The second and third have to be genuinely big: well above a typical week's scores, or covered by two or more outlets.

title: Importing Bandcamp ZIPs in a Flutter music player: streams, zip slip and Finder junk
summary:
People who still buy music mostly get it as a ZIP. Bandcamp, Qobuz and most download shops hand you one archive per album. My offline music player, Clickwheel, could only import loose audio files, so the first thing a new user had to do was find an unzip tool on their phone. That is a bad first minute.

title: Grafana Labs’ First Executive Briefing Center Coming to Ginza
summary:
Grafana Labs does not have a headquarters office. Since its founding in 2014, it has been fully remote-first.

It began with three co-founders living on different continents, and today our team spans more than 50 countries.
From day one, the organization was designed with the assumption that everyone works remotely. Real-time meetings are kept to a minimum, information is shared through documentation, and we have cultivated a culture that trusts people to “work autonomously.” At its core lies the transparency and autonomy of open source.

And now, we are building the world’s first Executive Briefing Center (EBC) in Ginza, Tokyo.

A remote-first company creating a physical space—what does that mean?
This article is the first in a three-part series following the EBC launch project.
From the background of the concept to site selection, design philosophy, and even the demolition process, we will walk you through the journey.
